{{short description|American composer, a pianist, and, mathematician}}
[[File:Leonard Sarason 1977.jpg|thumb|right|Leonard Sarason in 1977]]
'''Leonard Sarason''' (1925 – September 24, 1994) was a music composer, a pianist, and a mathematician. He earned a master's degree music composition from [[Yale University]], supervised by [[Paul Hindemith]].<ref name="uw">[https://www.washington.edu/alumni/columns/march95/obits0395.html In memory 3/95], Univ. of Washington, retrieved 2015-02-12.</ref><ref name="ibiblio">The Al Goldstein collection in the Pandora Music repository at http://www.ibiblio.org/pandora/mp3/contrib/Martha_Goldstein_Live/Readme</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Loving and Hating Mathematics: Challenging the Myths of Mathematical Life|first1=Reuben|last1=Hersh|first2=Vera|last2=John-Steiner|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2010|isbn=9781400836116|page=80|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gvsHAnAuIp4C&pg=PA80}}.</ref> After a doctorate in Mathematics at [[New York University]] supervised by [[Kurt Otto Friedrichs]]<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=33445}}</ref> he taught mathematics at [[Stanford University]] and the [[University of Washington]].<ref name="uw"/><ref name="ibiblio"/> His mathematical research concerned [[partial differential equation]]s.<ref name="uw"/>
